q: What is the energy use and CO2 of the Bankura secondary steel cluster in West Bengal?
title: Bankura secondary steel: energy and CO2
short: About 5.96 million t CO2 a year, by TERI's 2025 profile. Bankura's 37 or so units (sponge iron, ferro alloy, induction furnace and re-rolling) burn 1.61 million t of coal and use 4,246 million kWh, about 1.09 million toe, for some 3.6 million t of product.
audience: Sponge iron, ferro alloy, steel melting and re-rolling units in Bankura district, West Bengal

ul: Sponge iron (DRI): 10 units, 13,96,500 t a year, coal-fired rotary kilns.
Ferro alloy: 11 units, 3,06,740 t, submerged arc furnaces.
Induction furnace steel melting: 11 units, 12,63,600 t of ingots and billets.
Re-rolling: 5 units, 6,32,966 t of TMT bars, rods and angles.
Power comes from DVC or WBSEDCL; coal is both domestic and imported.
DRI: 1.53 million t of coal, 2.87 million t CO2. Coal is 66% of the cluster's energy, almost all of it in the kilns.
Ferro alloy: 2,883 million kWh, two thirds of the cluster's electricity, and 2.2 million t CO2 from only 8% of the output.
Induction furnaces: 1,200 million kWh, 0.86 million t CO2.
Re-rolling: 51 million kWh, 0.036 million t CO2.
Waste heat power on a 2 x 100 tpd DRI plant: about 5 MW, 23.5 million kWh a year and 16,685 t CO2 avoided, for about Rs 500 million.
Better kiln lining on a 100 tpd kiln: about 580 t of coal and 1,050 t CO2 a year.
Clean, dry scrap and full-power melting in induction furnaces: 5 to 10% of electricity.

sections.h: If billets or DRI go abroad
p: DRI, billets and bars are CBAM goods. For iron and steel, CBAM counts direct emissions only, so kiln coal decides a DRI figure and an induction furnace's power is left out, though both still count in a buyer's own footprint.

example.title: CO2 per tonne by unit type (from the profile)
lines: DRI: 2.87 million t CO2 / 1.40 million t = 2.06 t CO2 per tonne (about 1.1 t coal and 80 kWh)
Ferro alloy: 2.2 / 0.307 = 7.2 t CO2 per tonne (about 9,400 kWh)
Induction furnace billet: 0.86 / 1.26 = 0.68 t CO2 per tonne (about 950 kWh)
Re-rolling: 0.036 / 0.633 = 0.06 t CO2 per tonne (about 80 kWh)
Check: 1.61 million t coal x 1.76 + 4,246 million kWh x 0.675 = about 5.7 million t
example.note: Quantities and CO2 from TERI's 2025 Bankura profile; the check uses India's coal factor and CEA FY 2025-26. A bar made from DRI melted in an induction furnace carries the stages it passed through.

senseible: Senseible reads coal invoices (1.76 t CO2 a tonne Indian, 2.44 imported) and DVC or WBSEDCL bills into monthly records; the CBAM pages show what a direct-emissions figure means for an EU buyer.
